title: China-to-Iceland EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Redesign — IEC 62196 Type 2 and CCS2
rows.target_requirement: Iceland is a European-market EV context, so conductive charging hardware typically aligns to IEC 62196 Type 2 for AC and CCS2 for DC where project procurement and fleet requirements call for it. Connector alignment is an interoperability and tender requirement and is handled separately from the core electrical safety test result.
target_standards: Project, fleet, operator, or procurement connector requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China often uses GB/T 20234.2 and GB/T 20234.3 hardware and signaling for AC/DC connectors. These provide useful starting data but cannot be claimed as Type 2 or CCS2 compliance without hardware, cable, communication, and safety rebuild.
rows.gap: GB/T-only charger hardware needs connector and protocol migration for Iceland-facing deployment: coupler type selection, cable thermal rating, locking circuit, proximity and control pilot logic, DC communication if CCS2 is used, labels, and test evidence after migration.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where deployment contracts, charging fleet, or operator policy requires Type 2 / CCS2 compatibility; otherwise treated as interoperability expectation
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 20234 evidence is not direct Type 2 or CCS2 conformance

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not describe a GB/T-only connector package as Iceland Type 2 or CCS2 ready. Rebuild interface hardware, labeling, and safety documentation for the targeted Iceland deployment.

rows.target_requirement: Iceland chargers are reviewed based on location, voltage class, operation mode, and site-grid arrangement. For projects requiring grid use, evidence is needed for Landsnet interconnection route, metering and protection coordination, distribution-company correspondence, and commissioning acceptance with the project operator.
target_standards: Orkustofnun electricity market and licensing framework
Project electrical design and commissioning requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China deployment evidence often includes utility interconnection and commissioning records, but these follow Chinese technical rules and should not be reused as-is for Iceland grid-side acceptance.
china_standards: China utility interconnection and commissioning procedures
rows.gap: The gap is usually a clean separation of product scope from site operation scope. Prepare local connection notices, permit references, distribution-company acceptance criteria, metering integration, protection settings, and station energisation sequencing for each planned Iceland site.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the station uses public grid connection or regulated project delivery requirements in Iceland
mandatory_status.cn: China commissioning documents are not direct proof of Iceland grid acceptance

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not treat product conformity documents as complete charging-site readiness proof. Add site-specific Iceland grid and operator approvals before claiming operational readiness.

rows.requirement: Iceland Market Placement and CE Scope
rows.target_requirement: For EV chargers, Iceland uses EEA-aligned market placement logic for in-scope products. LVD, EMC, RED, and related safety obligations are expected where applicable; label and documentation must align to import-market role and operator model. EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 may additionally apply to battery-equipped systems and associated logistics and stewardship evidence.
target_standards: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries and waste batteries
rows.china_equivalent: China EV charger materials such as GB/T 18487 and domestic conformance reports support technical comparison, but do not by themselves establish Iceland market-access readiness or EEA CE scope fulfillment.
rows.gap: The market gap is documentary and route-based: importer obligations, declaration of conformity, labeling, warnings, EMC and safety declarations, RED module review, and O&M responsibility in the Iceland context.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where model scope includes EU-aligned directive coverage and public charging service operation expectations
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T documentation is a useful baseline but not a direct market-placement substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Validate Iceland-facing route before shipment. EV charger compliance claims should be backed by model-specific CE scope mapping, importer documentation, and site-operating documentation.

source.publisher: EUR-Lex and EEA Market Alignment references

rows.target_requirement: Iceland charging operations may require OCPP for backend interoperability, while electrical evidence remains model-scoped under CE-aligned LVD and EMC obligations. OCPP version, security profile, certificate handling, and interface mapping should be confirmed against the chosen operator and service process for the site.
target_standards: IEC 61000 series EMC requirements for grid and communication resilience
rows.china_equivalent: China often relies on GB/T 27930 for EV charger BMS communication, which is useful for battery interface proof, but it does not replace OCPP version, operator backend compliance, cybersecurity, or station integration evidence required by Iceland operators.
rows.gap: Map site backend requirements before shipment: OCPP endpoint model, security profile, transaction model, remote firmware method, certificate and key lifecycle, and EMC test evidence for communication electronics.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where operator, roaming, payment, or maintenance specification requires OCPP and where EMC evidence is part of acceptance criteria
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is not equivalent to OCPP or Iceland operator interoperability obligations

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm OCPP requirements against the operating entity before shipment. GB/T 27930 support is not sufficient for Iceland backend interoperability.

rows.requirement: EMC, Low-Voltage Safety, and Residual-Current Protection
rows.target_requirement: Iceland-ready EV chargers must support CE-aligned electrical safety and EMC obligations for in-scope equipment. IEC 61851-1 is a core EVSE safety reference, and EMC coverage should be mapped to applicable EMC routes including installation assumptions such as earthing, RCD design, overcurrent protection, and DC leakage response.
target_standards: IEC 61851-21-2 for off-board conductive charging EMC
rows.china_equivalent: China files may include GB/T 18487.1 and GB/T 18487.2 safety and EMC reports, which can support technical review. They are not a direct substitute for Iceland CE-aligned market placement and site-level protection assumptions.
rows.gap: Differences often occur in site protection design: RCD type, earth architecture, leakage thresholds, upstream breaker setting, surge coordination, EMC cable routing, short-circuit rating, ambient and ingress protection, and Turkish language instructions for warnings and response actions.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where in-scope CE-aligned low-voltage and EMC rules apply and where installation design requires local protection and residual-current design review
mandatory_status.cn: China safety/EMC reports are useful references but do not replace Iceland CE acceptance of site-level protection assumptions

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Use China GB/T safety and EMC outputs as technical baseline only. Confirm Iceland-focused residual-current and earthing assumptions against site design and operator acceptance before commissioning.
